## Objective

Connect native tools and helpers through consistent category-specific instructions.

## Scope

- Input normalization and manager handoff
- Generic, complex and extra-complex paths
- Implementation and integrated completion
- Stopping and navigation

## Entry conditions

- Storage and role APIs exist and are validated against their documented contracts.

## Exit criteria

- Active source instructions cover all paths and authority boundaries with actual helper syntax.

## Risks

- Partial instruction replacement can retain contradictory ownership or fork rules; reconcile the complete mapped contract.

## TASK-018 - Define independent complex candidates and senior fusion

### Risks

- None

### Acceptance criteria

- At least two solver instances receive the same versioned complete problem with suitable distinct perspectives; initial and queued contexts exclude sibling drafts.
- One distinct senior receives every required current candidate and fuses compatible contributions with traceable omissions and resolved differences; complex work adds no mandatory reviewer stage.
- An unresolved conflict returns the identical shared explanation to all solvers. Revised or versioned revalidated candidates form a consistent next set before synthesis.
- The senior returns to the manager for exact-proposal acceptance; contradiction, unchanged failure, or unavailable independence stops the cycle honestly.

### Planned verification

- Trace candidate packet and result-routing examples through the typed helper events and role-fit records.
- Review complementary, terminology, scope, evidence and mutually exclusive differences; reject voting, concatenation or hidden discarded opposition.

## TASK-019 - Define extra-complex review and conflict recycling

Specify one distinct reviewer per solver and current-version review gating for every extra-complex solution cycle.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | `completed` |
| State reason | None |
| Skip authority | None |
| Requirements | REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-019, REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-031 |

| Dependencies | TASK-018 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | 2026-09-08T09:27:18.793680Z |

### Risks

- None

### Acceptance criteria

- Each solver has its own reviewer instance; self-review and a reviewer shared by different solvers are rejected even if their role definitions are reusable.
- Evidenced mandatory defects return to the original solver and the current revision receives the assigned reviewer pass before eligibility.
- A synthesis conflict reaches all solvers; each current revised or revalidated candidate receives current review, and all passes bind to the new context before synthesis.
- Unavailable reviewer replacement preserves identity mapping/history; no stale pass, manager override, or optional improvement bypasses or indefinitely prolongs review.

### Planned verification

- Walk a rejection/revision/pass cycle and a synthesis-conflict/review/fusion cycle with exact version and reviewer mappings.
- Check missing, rejected, blocked, stale and mixed-baseline candidates all prevent senior dispatch.

## TASK-020 - Define conditional implementation and integrated completion

Specify exact manager acceptance, one dedicated implementation child for authorized multi-solution changes, and main-Task completion evidence.

### Risks

- None

### Acceptance criteria

- An implementation instance for complex/extra-complex work differs from manager, solvers, reviewers and senior and owns the exact accepted solution alone.
- Analysis objectives stop at a satisfactory accepted deliverable; coding objectives require performed changes. A design defect returns to the manager and invalidates affected acceptance.
- The manager inspects live outputs, interfaces, protected state and criterion evidence, and alone records truthful final Task completion.
- Contract, fixture, native runtime and end-to-end evidence are separately labeled; partial or unexercised native behavior cannot support broader completion claims.

### Planned verification

- Compare analysis-only, generic coding, complex coding and extra-complex coding handoffs with implementation-owner and action-authority criteria.
- Reject evidence-only child completion and check integration conflicts reopen affected decisions with current artifact references.
